text: DSH Plugin Tavily（DSH 网页插件）：将 Tavily 网页搜索接入 DSH 的 web provider，并在 Web 设置的插件页面提供双语配置卡片。它可按查询参数搜索网页、选择新闻或财经主题、限制结果域名和时间范围，并把摘要与来源交给 DSH；还可选用 Tavily Extract 或 Firecrawl 抓取页面。卡片支持设置凭据、搜索参数、测试连接和查看用量状态，适合需要联网检索或读取网页内容的 DSH 用户。使用 Tavily 搜索需配置 Tavily 凭据；Firecrawl 抓取需另配凭据，提取功能须选择对应 provider。

DSH Plugin Tavily adds Tavily web search and a bilingual settings card. It supports search filters, summaries, and optional page retrieval via Tavily Extract or Firecrawl. The card edits settings, tests connectivity, and shows usage. Each service may require its own credential.

DSH Plugin Tavily 的功能「可配置搜索参数」：通过插件配置和 Web 设置卡片调整主题、深度、结果数、日期窗口及域名过滤等请求选项。
DSH Plugin Tavily 的功能「网页内容提取」：注册 Tavily Extract 与可选 Firecrawl 抓取 provider；配置并选择相应 fetch provider 后可从 URL 获取页面内容。
DSH Plugin Tavily 的功能「设置卡片与状态」：Web 插件卡片编辑搜索配置和凭据，测试 API 连接并展示凭据对应的用量状态。

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · dsh-plugin-tavily：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A [Tavily](https://tavily.com)-backed **web search provider plugin** for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). It is the **professional/pro-user edition**: it exposes the full Tavily request parameter set through the web GUI, while still letting developers pin values from the profile configuration file.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · dsh-plugin-tavily：It registers a `tavily` search provider into the harness's `ctx.web` seam, so the built-in `web_search` tool searches the web through Tavily — and ships a **settings card** in the web GUI (`设置 → 插件 → 网页搜索`) where you paste your API key, tune advanced parameters, and test connectivity. One install, both halves.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Features：- **Install-and-use (no manual config)**: installing this plugin **auto-selects Tavily as the `web_search` provider** via its `cordis.patch.yml`. Paste a key in the card and search — no yaml or `DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER` edits required.
- **Tavily/DeepSeek engine switch**: a GUI switch answers `web_search` with Tavily (default; keyless if no key) or falls back to the **official DeepSeek** provider — no uninstall needed. This is a real provider-switch UI, not a config file edit.
- **Server-side connectivity probe**: `POST /api/tavily-probe` lets the card test a **stored** key (browsers cannot read stored secrets), using keyless mode when none is set.
- **Status indicator**: a `GET /api/tavily-status` route reads the stored key and Tavily `GET /usage` (no search credits) and the card shows a live ✅/⚠️/❌ badge (normal / credits low / API error, or "no key"), refreshed by the host without re-entering the key.
- **Full professional parameter set in the GUI**: API key, API Base URL, `maxResults`, `searchDepth` (basic/advanced/fast/ultra-fast), `topic`, `includeAnswer`, `includeRawContent`, `timeout`, `days`, `chunksPerSource`, `timeRange`, `s

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Install：Requires **dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer** (see [Requirements](#requirements)). Install from npm:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily"
```

During development, install from a local path instead:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "file:/absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-tavily"
```

Or from the repository's main branch (every merged commit):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:1624318455/dsh-plugin-tavily#main"
```

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Install：The plugin's `cordis.patch.yml` already sets `web.config.searchProvider: tavily`, so installing it **elects Tavily as the search provider for you** — no manual provider selection needed.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Enable：1. **Install & restart dsh.** The plugin's `cordis.patch.yml` already sets `web.config.searchProvider: tavily`, so Tavily is elected automatically — **no manual provider selection needed**.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Enable：2. **Set the Tavily API key** (optional). Open `设置 → 插件 → 网页搜索`, expand the **Web search (Tavily)** card, and paste the key into the **API key** field. Without a key Tavily runs **keyless** (free, rate-limited); with a key it uses your account tier. Choose the **Web search engine** switch: `tavily` (default) or `official DeepSeek`.

3. Use `web_search` as usual. The model-facing tool is unchanged; only the backend answering it is now Tavily (or DeepSeek, if you switched).

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Enable：> If you ever override the provider in yaml by hand, this is the row:

```yaml

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml：- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: tavily
```

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Enable the fetch (Extract) provider (optional)：The plugin also registers a Tavily Extract-backed **fetch** provider (`tavily-extract`) for reading a full page's content from a URL. It is inert until selected — set the fetch provider the same way as the search provider:

```sh
export DSH_WEB_FETCH_PROVIDER=tavily-extract
```

or, in `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: web
  config:
    searchProvider: tavily
    fetchProvider: tavily-extract

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Enable the fetch (Extract) provider (optional)：To use the optional **Firecrawl** page retriever instead (own key required — default credential reference `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`):

```sh
export DSH_WEB_FETCH_PROVIDER=firecrawl
```

or `fetchProvider: firecrawl` in the same `cordis.patch.yml` row. Without a Firecrawl key the provider reports `WEB_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_MISSING` on a fetch and stays inert otherwise.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Verify the backend is really Tavily：The `web_search` tool's output schema is provider-agnostic — the model never sees a provider name, and the API key intentionally lives outside environment variables, so "check the env" is the wrong probe. To confirm the active backend:

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Verify the backend is really Tavily：- **Provider selection** — `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` has the `web` row with `searchProvider: tavily`.
- **Plugin loaded** — the composed profile tree lists the `web-search-tavily` entry (`dsh --profile web --dump-config`).
- **Credential in place** — `TAVILY_API_KEY` exists in the credentials store (`~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`), not in the environment.
- **Result fingerprint** — a Tavily result carries a generated-answer summary in `content`; the built-in DeepSeek provider does not produce one.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · 🖥️ GUI usage (recommended for most users)：Every control has a short hint and a placeholder showing the default. Values are saved with the card's **Save** button and apply live; no service restart is needed.

> If a field shows **"Covered by config file; edit the yaml to change"**, it is pinned by `cordis.patch.yml` — the WebUI deliberately does not allow overriding it.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · ⚙️ Config-file usage (developer/pro users)：Configuration lives in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`). Add a `web-search-tavily` row with a `config` block:

```yaml
- id: web-search-tavily
  name: '@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily'
  config:
    searchDepth: advanced

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Priority：```
cordis.patch.yml config  >  WebUI card values  >  code defaults
```

- If a key is present in the yaml `config` block, the card disables that field and shows the configuration-covered badge.
- If the yaml does not set a field, the WebUI value (if any) is used.
- If neither sets it, the code default applies.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Settings table：`apiKeyEnv` stays config-only deliberately: it is an advanced wiring detail. Values saved from the GUI land in the profile's `web-search-tavily` entry (`~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`). Settings edits apply live — the provider re-reads the section for every operation, so no restart or re-registration is needed after changing a value from the card or the file.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Requirements：- **dsh 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer.** The plugin targets the 0.2.x plugin API: the settings form is declared by marking the plugin's `Config` schema fields `.volatile()`, the card reads its section through `ctx.configForms`, and the card registers into the Plugins page's `plugins.item` slot. Older 0.1.x runtimes used a different settings contract and are not supported.
- **Tavily API key** — paste it into the card, or store `TAVILY_API_KEY` in the credentials store.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Platform note (web GUI card visibility)：**No patch is needed on dsh 0.2.x.** Earlier releases (0.1.x) served a plugin's settings section to the browser only when its namespace was on the apiproxy allowlist, so a third-party card had to be unblocked by hand. That mechanism is gone: the 0.2.x settings domain serves any plugin entry that declares a volatile config schema, and the card registers itself under the Plugins page.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Platform note (web GUI card visibility)：The card appears in **设置 → 插件** as **网页搜索（Tavily）** once the plugin is installed and dsh is restarted. It is hidden while the host half is not loaded — the card's registration follows the host's own serving of the `web-search-tavily` namespace.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Platform note (web GUI card visibility)：> **Server-side test of a stored key.** This plugin registers a host probe `POST /api/tavily-probe` that can test Tavily with a **stored** key server-side (keyless when none is set); `TavilySearchProvider.connectivityTest()` / `probe()` / `usage()` / `status()` are the programmatic host-side paths, and `GET /api/tavily-status` backs the card's status indicator. The browser cannot read stored secrets back, so the card's `Test API connection` button still requires re-entering an already-configured key.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Mapping：Tavily's flat `results[]` maps to normalized `WebSearchSource`s: `url` ← `url`, `title` ← `title`, `snippet` ← the non-blank `content` (entries without content are dropped), `publishedAt` ← `published_date` (news/finance topics). Tavily's generated `answer` (when `includeAnswer`) becomes the result `content`. A request's `maxResults` wins over the configured default and is sent as Tavily's `max_results`; the seam enforces the final bound. The full professional request set is forwarded: `search_depth` (basic/advanced/fast/ultra-fast), `chunks_per_source`, `topic`, `time_range`, `start_date`/`end_date`, `days`, `include_answer` (boolean or `basic`/`advanced`), `include_raw_content` (boolean or `markdown`/`text`), `include_images`, `include_image_descriptions`, `include_favicon`, `include_domains`/`exclude_domains`, and `country`. Note: `include_images`/`include_favicon` are sent to Tavily but cannot yet be surfaced through the normalized `WebSearchSource` shape (the seam has no image/favicon field); they are exposed so the request can carry them. Failures surface as the seam's `WebError` (`WEB_PROVIDER_ERROR` / `WEB_ABORTED`); request tim

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Roadmap (planned)：Deferred (deliberately, see the optimization review): **search-then-extract (top-N pages)** would change result semantics (extracted text must be injected into `content`), burn extract credits per URL, and implicitly couple search to full-page retrieval — revisit as a separate opt-in feature if users ask.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Development：```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build          # tsdown → lib/index.mjs (host) + lib/client.cjs (browser, committed)
pnpm run typecheck      # tsc --noEmit
pnpm run test:contract  # slot-contract drift guard (no network)

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Development：The **browser E2E** (`tests/browser-e2e.mjs`) is the layer that reproduces the
loader-failure scenario: it boots a real `dsh web`, drives the first-run wizard
in a real browser, and asserts the plugin loads — the "Failed to load plugins /
list slot requires options.id" banner is the exact symptom it fails on. Used by
the CI `browser-e2e` matrix; the headless Chrome stall it can hit on loaded dev
machines is handled by per-phase time budgets, a 300s watchdog, and a retry in CI.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Development：The card's slot contract is the dsh 0.2.x one: the Plugins page declares
`plugins.item` as a **list** slot (registration requires `id`), and the card
registers with `id` + `order` + a localized `label`. `pnpm run test:contract`
parses the shipped `lib/client.cjs` and feeds its registration shape into the
real `SlotCore` under that declaration; the CI matrix
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) reruns it against the published
`dsh-client-ui-slots` cores (`0.2.0-rc.2` / `0.2.1-rc.2`) and boots a real dsh
profile per release to verify the served bundle.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Development：The slot-contract section above is pinned by `pnpm run test:contract` and the
CI matrix. **Releases are fully automated and CI-gated**: bump `package.json`
version and push to `main` — the `Release` workflow
(`.github/workflows/release.yml`) waits for that commit's CI run to finish
green, then tags `v<version>`, publishes a GitHub Release with generated
changelog and the packed tarball, and **publishes the package to npm** through
Trusted Publishing (OIDC + provenance — no npm secret lives in the repository).
Cadence is SemVer-driven: **patch** for bug fixes (especially issue-anchored
ones — someone is waiting), **minor** for feature batches, **major** for
breaking changes. The `#main` install path delivers every merged commit
regardless; tags are the immutable "recommended version" snapshots.

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Development：> **npm Trusted Publishing setup (one-time, by a package admin).**
> npmjs.com → the package → Settings → Trusted Publisher → GitHub Actions:
> organization/user `1624318455`, repository `dsh-plugin-tavily`, workflow
> filename `release.yml`, environment empty. After that, publishing needs no
> secret. The first publish must create the package under the
> `@memef1f1y` scope, so run `npm publish --access public` once by hand if

@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-tavily README · Development：`lib/` is committed so the plugin installs without a build step (no `prepare` script, no pnpm build-script allowlisting). The `@deepseek-ai/*` seam and framework packages are **externalized** — the harness provides them at runtime, declared as `peerDependencies`. The browser bundle (`lib/client.cjs`) is a CJS module-loader factory: it `require()`s only the client module table's platform packages and inlines the plugin's own card code, so it needs no extra install-time resolution. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` is a devDependency only, so the smoke test can resolve the harness runtime closure.
